title: An Evaluation of a Hydrophilic Intermittent Urinary Catheter in Adult Male and Female Patients
official: An Open, Non-controlled, Interventional, Multicenter Clinical Investigation to Evaluate the Clinical Safety and Performance of a Hydrophilic Intermittent Urinary Catheter (New LoFric Male and LoFric Elle Pro) in Adult Male and Female Patients
summary:
This study is being conducted to evaluate the safety and clinical performance of two new catheters for intermittent catheterisation in female/male adults (≥18 years).

The main question it aims to answer is to evaluate complete bladder emptying during intermittent catheterisation.

The study involves two visits to the study clinic over 14 days. During the study only the study catheters will be used and catheterise according to normal routine and not use any other catheters. Subject will be in close contact with the site personnel and must follow their instructions. This is to ensure that the evaluation regarding your experience of the study catheter will be as accurate as possible.

The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency and the Research Ethics Committee have reviewed and approved the study.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Subject given assent to take part in the clinical investigation, i.e. understand and sign the Informed Consent Form.
2. Adult (male/female), aged ≥18 years at the time of inclusion.
3. Suffering from bladder voiding dysfunction.
4. Experienced practitioner of intermittent catheterization defined as a minimum of one month on therapy.
5. Practice intermittent catheterization at least 3 times daily.
6. Using catheters in the sizes available in the investigation (CH 12 or CH 14).
7. The subject is able to read, write, and understand the information given to them regarding the clinical investigation.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Ongoing, symptomatic urinary tract infection (UTI) at enrolment as judged by investigator. The definition of UTI is a positive urine culture of ≥103 CFU/ml of ≥1 bacterial species and presence of symptoms or signs compatible with UTI.
2. Known urethral stricture which, in the opinion of the investigator, could influence the subject's evaluation of the catheters.
3. Urodynamic procedures have been conducted during the past two weeks.
4. Bladder Botulinum toxin treatment during past 7 days.
5. Involvement in the planning and conduct of the investigation (applies to both Wellspect HealthCare staff and site staff).
6. Previous enrolment in the present clinical investigation.
7. Simultaneous participation in another clinical investigation that may impact the primary endpoint.
8. Expected or severe non-compliance to the Clinical Investigation Plan (CIP), as judged by the investigator.
